sources.pathloss: 3GPP TR 38.901 Table 7.4.1-1 RMa (h=5 m, W=20 m), LOS probability Table 7.4.2-1; chosen after deneyler/20
sources.dl_earfcn: CellMapper, Turkcell B3 primary carrier observed on Balikesir towers (17.11.2026)
sources.enb_power: 3GPP TR 36.814 Table A.2.1.1-1: 49 dBm for a 20 MHz carrier
sources.beamwidth: 3GPP TR 36.814/36.942 sector antenna, 65 deg horizontal HPBW
sources.vertical_pattern: 3GPP TR 36.814 vertical pattern form, 10 deg HPBW, 20 dB cap
sources.distance_correction: deneyler/22 method re-derived for the 3GPP antenna (correction.py)
sources.antenna_pattern: 3GPP TR 36.814 Table A.2.1.1-2: A=min(A_H+A_V,25), A_H cap 25, A_V cap 20; chosen after deneyler/22
sources.load_factor: KPI mean DL PRB 0.233, calibrated on draw 701 (calibration/)

correction.rule:
- Context: deneyler/22 derived extra_loss(d) = RSRP_model(d) - RSRP_Experia(d) with the cosine antenna. In
  deneyler/23-24 the antenna became the 3GPP pattern but the correction was not re-derived, and RSRP got worse
  (held-out 3.5 -> 5.4 dB). deneyler/25 showed the missing SINR ceiling (transmitter EVM). All of this was
  seen before designing deneyler/26; reported as such.
- Same method as deneyler/22, applied to the 3GPP-antenna model:
  * RSRP_Experia(d): unchanged fit from deneyler/22 (Experia cells of the region, 8 evaluation sites excluded).
  * RSRP_model(d): fit a + b*log10(d) over the measured users of the three deneyler/24 LC_TA runs, using the
    UNCORRECTED RSRP = simulated RSRP + that user's deneyler/22 extra_loss_db. This is exact, because the
    correction is the same on every link of a user (verified in deneyler/22: RSRP change = -extra_loss,
    correlation 1.0) and RSRP does not depend on load or EVM. d = serving distance, clipped 100 m-15 km.
    Only simulation output is used; no Experia value of the evaluation sites.
  * New extra_loss(d) = RSRP_model(d) - RSRP_Experia(d), applied per user as before (measured users: TA
    placement distance; load users: distance to target site).
- Load intervals are copied from deneyler/24 (factor 1.243) and re-calibrated by calibrate.py.

load_calibration.rule:
- Radio: deneyler/24 (RMa, 3GPP antenna, 8 dB shadow, ...) + transmitter EVM 8 % (3GPP TS 36.104) + the
  distance correction re-derived by correction.py (inputs/ues_EC_TA_*.csv). EVM lowers SINR and therefore
  spectral efficiency, so the load giving KPI PRB changes.
- Target is the measured load only: mean DL PRB = 0.233. SINR, RSRP or CQI are NOT used.
- Same method as deneyler/14 and /24: only draw 701. Load-user UDP interval = factor / 0.233 ms.
  Round 1: factor = 1.2432 (the deneyler/24 factor). If round-1 PRB is within 0.233 +/- 5 % it is frozen;
  otherwise one proportional step (factor * PRB_round1 / 0.233) is taken and frozen without further checks.

rule:
- Question: how many simultaneous voice calls can each cell of the 8 evaluation sites carry before calls
  fail, and how does that compare with the KPI's normal and earthquake-time number of connected users?
- Model: identical to deneyler/26 FT_TA (RMa, 3GPP antenna, EVM 8 % in the private libns3-lte, distance
  correction, 8 dB shadow, frozen load factor 1.243). Only the users change. SRS periodicity is set to 320
  so that up to 320 UEs can attach to one cell (ns-3 default allows far fewer); this does not change radio.
- Users:
  * Background data: the 72 load users of deneyler/26 unchanged (normal-day KPI load, PRB ~0.23). Kept
    constant at every step; during the earthquakes the KPI data volume actually fell by about one third,
    so this is on the conservative side.
  * Voice: N voice users per cell, i.e. 3N per evaluation site (3 sectors), placed like the measured users
    of deneyler/15/26: distance from a random hourly Experia TA record of that site (TAAVG x 4.88 m,
    100 m-15 km), uniformly random direction, extra_loss_db from the deneyler/26 correction formula.
    Each voice user receives an AMR 12.2 kbps call: one packet every 20 ms (3GPP TS 26.114), UDP payload
    44 bytes (32 B speech frame + 12 B RTP), 72 B at IP level (28.8 kbps). Neighbour sites get no voice
    users (they stay at normal load and act as interference).
  * Steps N = 25, 50, 100, 200, 300 voice users per cell (300 is just under the 320 SRS limit). The same N
    is used for every evaluation cell, so each cell's capacity is read directly; the KPI number of connected
    users per cell (normal and x2 for the earthquake signature) is compared with it afterwards.
- Criteria (3GPP / ITU, fixed before the runs):
  * A voice user "can talk" if >= 99 % of its packets sent in the measurement window arrive within 100 ms
    (3GPP TS 23.203 QCI 1: 100 ms delay budget, 1 % packet loss; TS 26.132 Annex E: 99 % within budget).
  * A cell "carries" its load if >= 98 % of the voice users served by it can talk (VoIP-capacity convention
    of 3GPP TR 25.814 / ITU-R M.2135; to be checked against the documents before it is cited).
  * "No service": a voice user that is not RRC-connected at the end.
  * Measurement window: packets sent between 1 s (warm-up) and duration - 0.25 s.
- Runs: one azimuth draw (42, UE seed 701) for all steps because of run time; the step around the capacity
  limit and N = 2 x KPI may be repeated with draws 7/702 and 99/703 afterwards. 4 s per run.
- Regression first: with the new options unused the simulator must reproduce deneyler/16
  regression_disabled_draw701 byte for byte (after CRLF->LF).
